sent_to_model:
I want to post a review of an old ninja movie I watched on Starz last night. My friends and I were obsessed with ninjas as kids, and I went to see this one several times back then. Watching it again was hilarious. Can you help me write about why I enjoyed it so much despite how ridiculous it is? I want to share the childhood connection and the scenes that cracked me up, especially the farm celebration, the gangster's operation, and Cole's trip through headquarters to the final fight. I'd also like to cover the ending because that last business before the credits is just bizarre. Spoilers are fine.

- Watched on Starz last night; originally saw it repeatedly at the local theater as a child.
- Cole visits an old army friend, probably named Frank; gangsters want the friend's land.
- Sho Kosugi plays the rival ninja; remembered him from childhood.
- Early eighties setting and fashions: flares, large moustaches, Farrah hairstyles, ninja craze.
- The American gangster operates in the Phillipines; both he and his hired men dress in white suits.
- Cole wears an all-white ninja costume, including a face covering.
- Cockfighting facilities feature at the farm and at the villain's much larger arena.
- Sho holds Frank's wife captive; she is also romantically involved with Cole.
- Final duel ends with Cole winning and Sho receiving an honorable death through decapitation.
- Ending has Cole preparing to leave town, a threat involving an overweight hook-handed man, then a camera wink, frozen image and credits.
- Friends and I were really into ninjas when this came out.
- Possibly remember Kosugi's martial arts magazine advertisements claiming he alone was an authentic ninja; memory uncertain.
- Farmhands return after intimidation by hired muscle; Frank celebrates their return by proposing a cockfight, and everyone eagerly joins in.
- Frank repeatedly loses fights with the land-grabbing gang and spends much of the movie drinking; peculiar face and almost motionless jaw when speaking.
- Headquarters entry: secretary notices Cole, alerts security; guard discharges a pump-action shotgun very near the villains, who show no reaction.
- Cole climbs stairs trying to be stealthy, then somersaults into the enemy gathering; his movement looks awkward.
- Deputy says Cole's killing was unnecessary because his arrival was anticipated; then transports him to the arena.
- Cole arrives at the arena wearing his ninja mask.
- Sho releases the captive woman before the duel; the opponents bow and circle before fighting.
- Terrible filmmaking makes this extremely entertaining; affection mixed with disbelief.
- Kosugi's vocal noises and exaggerated ninja gestures are especially amusing.
- Fight doubles are conspicuous; lavish cockfighting venue and coordinated white outfits add to the absurdity.
- Give other viewers plenty of specific ridiculous moments and share the childhood nostalgia.

(About me: movie fan. Length: it should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

must_cover: Explain the enjoyment of the movie's ridiculous shortcomings.
Describe the writer's childhood enthusiasm for ninjas and repeated theater visits.
Recount the farm celebration, gangster operation, headquarters intrusion and final duel.
Describe the strange events immediately before the credits.
